diagnosticDetail: org.pytorch.executorch.llm.error error 32 (NotFound) during TextRunner.load() on iPhone 15 Pro (iOS 26.2.1). The iOS LLM runner calls module_->load_method("forward") (extension/llm/runner/text_decoder_runner.h). A strings scan of the PTE shows the literal "forward" IS present in the artifact, so a missing method name is NOT confirmed — error 32 (NotFound) can also originate at backend init, memory planning, or tensor resolution. Method-table inspection tooling is not available in this environment, so the exact missing resource is unverified. The model card and ExecuTorch docs describe this artifact as Android/ARM CPU (XNNPACK + KleidiAI) targeted with no iOS claims.
rationale: The SpinQuant INT4 PTE artifact fails to load on the ExecuTorch 1.3.1 iOS Swift LLM runner with error 32 (NotFound). The model card documents Android/ARM CPU benchmarking only, with no iOS claims. The precise load stage (method lookup vs. backend init vs. memory planning) is not isolated, and method-table inspection tooling is not available in this environment. The failure is consistent with an Android-targeted export being incompatible with the iOS Swift runner path, but the exact missing resource is unverified. This is not a device capability failure — the iPhone 15 Pro has sufficient RAM and the app pipeline works.

evidence.rootCauseSource: Unverified. ExecuTorch source shows load_method("forward") is the iOS runner entry point, but the PTE contains the string "forward". Error 32 stage not isolated.

upstreamReference: https://github.com/pytorch/executorch/blob/main/examples/models/llama/README.md — quantized models documented as Android/ARM CPU (XNNPACK + KleidiAI); no iOS load claims
remediation: Re-export the Llama 3.2 1B model for iOS using ExecuTorch export_llama.py with iOS-appropriate backend targets, use the BF16 baseline documented as iOS-compatible, or isolate the exact NotFound stage with ExecuTorch method-table tooling (not available in this environment).
